utterances.text: Ken Dickinson, San Rafael Meadows Mayor Council members this is a comment on 2a. Thank you for your recent letter for explaining your reasoning behind the current public comment structure. I respectfully and wholeheartedly disagree. However, the current approach prioritizes efficiency over what best practices show is essential to meaningful democratic participation. Across California, and especially here in Marin and Sonoma counties, many cities place non agenda public comment at the beginning of meetings. Sausalito, Mill Valley, Tiburon, San Anselmo, Fairfax, Novato, Sonoma, Petaluma, Santa Rosa, Sebastopol, Healdsburg, Cloverdale and the county of Morin all do this. Some allow up to 30 minutes at the start, with additional comment later if needed. This is a widely recognised best practice, adopted not because cities must, but because experience shows it improves access, equity and the quality of deliberation. Public comment serves a role that emails or private conversations cannot replace. It is public collective on the record. It allows residents to hear one another and raise shared concerns in the same forum where policy direction is discussed. When non agenda comment is pushed to the end of meetings, participation predictably declines among people with limited time, family responsibilities or long commutes. This is a chilling effect on public participation. Structure sends signals when public voices come first. It communicates that community concerns are foundational to the Council's work. It also strengthens decision making by providing context before positions harden. You and the council report to the electorate. Public participation is not an obstacle to good governments. It is one of its clearest measures. I respectfully request for the second time that non agenda public comment be moved back to the beginning of the agenda where it was prior to October 2nd.
